recommendation: Limit daily sodium intake to < 2,000 mg (approx. 5g table salt). Increase dietary potassium through whole vegetables and low-GI fruits unless contraindicated by renal disease.
Prioritize complex carbohydrates with low glycemic index (< 55). Distribute carbohydrate intake evenly across meals to prevent postprandial glucose spikes. Maintain daily fiber intake > 30g.

When weight plateaus for > 14 days on a consistent caloric deficit, re-evaluate TDEE based on current lower body mass. Introduce 2-day diet break at estimated maintenance calories to restore leptin and thyroid hormone (T3) levels.
Focus on high-protein (25-30% total energy), low-glycemic dietary patterns to improve insulin sensitivity. Limit refined sugars and emphasize anti-inflammatory omega-3 fatty acids.
For non-dialysis Chronic Kidney Disease, restrict dietary protein to 0.6-0.8 g/kg body weight. Monitor serum potassium, phosphorus, and sodium levels carefully.
Aim for a 7-10% total body weight reduction at a rate of 0.5-1.0 kg/week. Eliminate fructose-sweetened beverages and ultra-processed foods to reduce intrahepatic fat content.
Ensure adequate iodine and selenium intake for thyroid hormone synthesis. Allow at least a 4-hour window between thyroid medication administration and calcium/iron supplements or high-fiber meals.
